chapter_name: Vakya Vichar: Ang, Bhed, Aur Vakya Roopantaran (Syntax: Parts, Types, and Sentence Transformation)
learning_objective: 🎯 By the end of this chapter, you will learn how to arrange words perfectly to express complete thoughts, identify the hero of every sentence, and magically transform simple sentences into complex ones!

main_concepts.concept_title: 📝 What is a Vakya? (The Complete Thought)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: A bunch of random words thrown together is not a sentence! 'रहा है लड़का दौड़' makes no sense. A 'Vakya' is a group of words arranged in a specific grammatical order (Subject + Object + Verb in Hindi) that delivers a complete, logical meaning. Correct: 'लड़का दौड़ रहा है' (The boy is running).

Every sentence can be sliced in half. The 'Uddeshya' (Subject) is WHO or WHAT the sentence is about. The 'Vidheya' (Predicate) is what the subject is DOING or what is being said about it. In 'राम किताब पढ़ता है' (Ram reads a book), 'राम' is the Uddeshya, and 'किताब पढ़ता है' is the Vidheya.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🎭 Arth Ke Aadhar Par (Sentences by Meaning)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Based on what they express, sentences have 8 types! Examples: Vidhanvachak (Simple facts), Nishedhvachak (Negative/Saying NO), Prashnavachak (Asking questions), Agyavachak (Giving orders), and Vismayadibodhak (Expressing surprise!).

main_concepts.concept_title: 🧱 Rachna Ke Aadhar Par (Sentences by Structure)
main_concepts.simple_explanation:
Based on how they are built, sentences have 3 types. 
1. Saral (Simple) - One subject, one main verb. 
2. Sanyukt (Compound) - Two independent simple sentences joined by 'and/but' (और, परंतु). 
3. Mishra (Complex) - One main sentence and one dependent sentence joined by 'because/if/that' (कि, क्योंकि, यदि).

This is the art of changing a sentence from one type to another WITHOUT changing its core meaning! Example: 'सुबह होते ही पक्षी चहचहाने लगे' (Simple) can be transformed to 'सुबह हुई और पक्षी चहचहाने लगे' (Compound).

fun_activity.title: 🪄 The 'Sentence Shapeshifter' Trick
fun_activity.instructions: Take this simple positive sentence: 'मैं कल दिल्ली जाऊँगा' (I will go to Delhi tomorrow). Now, transform it! Change it into a Negative sentence (Nishedhvachak), a Question (Prashnavachak), and a Surprise (Vismayadibodhak) sentence. Write down all 3 forms!

quick_recap: ⭐ A Vakya (Sentence) is an ordered, meaningful group of words.
⭐ Every sentence has two main parts: Uddeshya (Subject) and Vidheya (Predicate).
⭐ Based on meaning (Arth), sentences are classified into 8 types (Questions, Negatives, Orders, etc.).
⭐ Based on structure (Rachna), sentences are Simple (Saral), Compound (Sanyukt), or Complex (Mishra).
⭐ Vakya Roopantaran means converting a sentence structure without losing its original meaning.
